Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to move forward, but our networking team flagged a concern: EdgeCorp will manage the colo edge peering and transit routers for the private deployment. During a recent load run we observed short, high-latency spikes that appear to originate on our WAN peering layer.

Before committing to a 99.95% tail latency SLO on production traffic, procurement asked whether Redwood can accept an appendix that limits uptime/latency attribution where the root cause is within EdgeCorp-controlled peering/transit. Concretely: when the issue is inside our peering fabric or our transit provider, we’d like those incidents excluded from Redwood uptime/latency calculations for SLA breach purposes.

I’ve attached a short trace set and a topology diagram to illustrate. Can you confirm what evidence you’d need to accept an exclusion and how we’d operationalize it (e.g., required flow logs, timestamps, point-of-failure attribution)?

Also looping in legal in case they want to start on language.

Carlos —

Appreciate the detail and the traces. Quick answers up front: we’re open to a scoped SLA amendment that attributes latency incidents to customer-controlled network segments, provided the incident evidence meets a few criteria and we have deterministic attribution logic.

High-level items we’ll need to proceed:
- A clear mapping of the customer-managed network segments and ownership (your topology helps).
- Time-synchronized traces and flow logs (sFlow/NetFlow) for the incident window.
- Confirmation that EdgeCorp transit provider will share corroborating logs on request (or a path to POC with the provider).
- An operational playbook: how incidents are triaged and what tickets/alerts are created.

Operationally, our suggestion is to implement a two-step process:
1) Initial triage and binary attribution (Redwood runtime vs customer network) using packet traces + connectivity checks.
2) For incidents attributed to customer fabric, provide an exclusion report within 72 hours. If the root cause is ambiguous, default to treating as Redwood-impacting until proven otherwise for a maximum of one major incident per quarter (to discourage under-reporting).

I’ve looped in Vivek to review the legal/ops constraints and Marissa so sales can align on procurement language. I’ll draft proposed amendment language once we confirm evidence types.

Best,

Thanks for the ping. High-level stance from product/ops: acceptable with controls. Proposed guardrails to include in the amendment and internal playbook:

- Evidence standard: timestamped packet captures + NetFlow/sFlow + traceroutes from both sides and evidence from the transit provider OR full BGP update logs showing flap/withdrawal correlated to the incident.
- Monitoring hooks: enable VPC flow logs and peer-side flow logs; agree on timezone/clock sync (NTP).
- Scheduled maintenance: EdgeCorp must publish planned maintenance windows 7 days in advance with a defined change window. Planned windows can be excluded; emergency maintenance must be documented within 24 hours to be considered for exclusion.
- Quantitative limits: allow up to 2 excluded incidents per rolling 12 months without Redwood adjusting SLO targets; beyond that we reserve right to re-evaluate the contract or require additional mitigations.
- Security/forensics: Redwood will retain the right to request sanitized logs for root-cause confirmation; any logs provided must remove customer-sensitive payloads.

I’ve drafted suggested amendment language and attached a working doc (sla-amendment-draft.docx). Legal will want to tighten the wording but this should speed things along.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product Operations
